value.zh: 世宗宣武帝
value.en: Emperor Shizong Xuanwu.
value.literal: Emperor Shizong Xuanwu.

value.zh: 宜遵舊典，稱詔宇內，以副黎蒸元元之望。」
value.en: We should follow precedent, proclaim the title throughout the realm, and answer the hopes of the common people."
value.literal: It is fitting to follow the old precedents, proclaim the title throughout the realm, and answer the hopes of the black-haired common people."

value.zh: 是月，改葬文昭皇太后高氏。
value.en: That month, Empress Dowager Wenzhao of the Gao clan was reburied.
value.literal: That month, Empress Dowager Wenzhao of the Gao clan was reburied.

value.zh: 二月乙丑，齊郡王祐薨。
value.en: In the second month, on the yichou day, You, Prince of Qi Commandery, died.
value.literal: In the second month, on the yichou day, You, Prince of Qi Commandery, died.

value.zh: 庚午，羽林千餘人焚征西將軍張彝第，毆傷彝，燒殺其子始均。
value.en: On the gengwu day, more than a thousand Feathered Forest guards burned the residence of Zhang Yi, General Who Conquers the West, beat and injured him, and burned his son Shijun to death.
value.literal: On the gengwu day, more than a thousand Feathered Forest guards burned the residence of Zhang Yi, General Who Conquers the West, beat and injured Yi, and burned his son Shijun to death.

value.zh: 乙亥，大赦。
value.en: On the yihai day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
value.literal: On the yihai day, there was a great amnesty.

value.zh: 丁丑，詔求直言。
value.en: On the dingchou day, an edict called for forthright criticism.
value.literal: On the dingchou day, an edict sought forthright speech.

value.zh: 壬寅，詔以旱故，命依舊雩祈，察理冤獄，掩胔埋骼，振窮恤寡。
value.en: On the renyin day, because of the drought, an edict ordered rain-prayers according to old practice, the review of wrongful imprisonments, the burial of exposed remains, and relief for the poor and widowed.
value.literal: On the renyin day, because of the drought, an edict ordered rain-prayers according to old practice, the investigation and correction of unjust imprisonments, the covering of exposed corpses and burial of bones, and relief for the poor and aid for widows.

value.zh: 三月甲辰，澍雨大洽。
value.en: In the third month, on the jiachen day, soaking rain fell in great abundance.
value.literal: In the third month, on the jiachen day, soaking rain fell in great abundance.

value.zh: 夏五月戊戌，以司空、任城王澄為司徒，京兆王繼為司空。
value.en: In summer, in the fifth month, on the wuxu day, Cheng, Minister of Works and Prince of Rencheng, was made Minister over the Masses, and Ji, Prince of Jingzhao, was made Minister of Works.
value.literal: In summer, in the fifth month, on the wuxu day, Cheng, Minister of Works and Prince of Rencheng, was made Minister over the Masses, and Ji, Prince of Jingzhao, was made Minister of Works.

value.zh: 秋八月乙未，御史中尉、東平王匡坐事削除官爵。
value.en: In autumn, in the eighth month, on the yiwei day, Kuang, Censor-in-Chief and Prince of Dongping, was stripped of office and noble rank for an offense.
value.literal: In autumn, in the eighth month, on the yiwei day, Kuang, Censor-in-Chief and Prince of Dongping, was implicated in an affair and stripped of office and noble rank.

value.zh: 九月庚寅，皇太后幸嵩高山。
value.en: In the ninth month, on the gengyin day, the Empress Dowager visited Mount Songgao.
value.literal: In the ninth month, on the gengyin day, the Empress Dowager visited Mount Songgao.

value.zh: 癸巳，還宮。
value.en: On the guisi day, she returned to the palace.
value.literal: On the guisi day, she returned to the palace.

value.zh: 冬十二月癸丑，司徒、任城王澄薨。
value.en: In winter, in the twelfth month, on the guichou day, Cheng, Minister over the Masses and Prince of Rencheng, died.
value.literal: In winter, in the twelfth month, on the guichou day, Cheng, Minister over the Masses and Prince of Rencheng, died.

value.zh: 庚申，大赦。
value.en: On the gengshen day, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
value.literal: On the gengshen day, there was a great amnesty.

value.zh: 詔除淫祀，焚諸雜神。
value.en: An edict abolished improper cults and burned assorted cult images.
value.literal: An edict abolished improper sacrifices and burned the various miscellaneous gods.

value.zh: 是歲，吐谷渾、宕昌、嚈噠等國並遣使朝貢。
value.en: That year, Tuyuhun, Dangchang, the Hephthalites, and other states all sent envoys to court with tribute.
value.literal: That year, Tuyuhun, Dangchang, Hephthalites, and other states all sent envoys to court with tribute.

value.zh: 劉焉字君郎，江夏竟陵人也，魯恭王後也。
value.en: Liu Yan, styled Junlang, came from Jingling in Jiangxia and traced his line to Prince Gong of Lu.
value.literal: Liu Yan, courtesy name Junlang, was a man of Jingling in Jiangxia, and a descendant of Prince Gong of Lu.

value.zh: 肅宗時，徙竟陵。
value.en: Under Emperor Suzong his clan was moved to Jingling.
value.literal: In the time of Emperor Suzong, the family was relocated to Jingling.

value.zh: 焉少任州郡，以宗室拜郎中。
value.en: As a young man he served in provincial posts and, by virtue of his imperial lineage, received appointment as a Gentleman of the Palace.
value.literal: In youth Yan held office in the provinces and commanderies, and as a member of the imperial clan was appointed Gentleman of the Palace.

value.zh: 去官居陽城山，精學教授。
value.en: He resigned, withdrew to Mount Yangcheng, pursued scholarship in earnest, and lectured to students.
value.literal: Leaving office, he dwelt on Mount Yangcheng, devoted himself to study, and taught.

value.zh: 舉賢良方正，稍遷南陽太守、宗正、太常。
value.en: Recommended as an outstanding candidate for honest and upright conduct, he rose step by step to governor of Nanyang, minister for the imperial clan, and minister of ceremonies.
value.literal: Recommended as Worthy and Good, Honest and Upright, he was gradually promoted to Governor of Nanyang, Minister of the Imperial Clan, and Minister of Ceremonies.

value.zh: 時，靈帝政化衰缺，四方兵寇，焉以為刺史威輕，既不能禁，且用非其人，輒增暴亂，乃建議改置牧伯，鎮安方夏，清選重臣，以居其任。
value.en: Under Emperor Ling government faltered and rebellion spread. Liu Yan argued that provincial inspectors lacked real authority—unable to keep order, and that wrong appointments only bred more chaos—so he urged installing chief administrators over the regions to stabilize the empire and staffing those offices with senior, carefully chosen ministers.
value.literal: At that time Emperor Ling's governance was decaying and flawed; armed bandits arose on every side. Yan held that the inspectors' authority was light: they could neither restrain trouble, and when the wrong men were appointed, violence only increased. He therefore proposed replacing them with regional shepherds, to pacify the realm, and selecting eminent ministers of proven weight to fill those posts.

value.zh: 焉乃陰求為交阯，以避時難。
value.en: He quietly angled for a posting to Jiaozhi, hoping to ride out the turmoil at a distance.
value.literal: Yan then secretly sought appointment to Jiaozhi, to escape the troubles of the age.

value.zh: 議未即行，會益州刺史郗儉在政煩擾，謠言遠聞，而并州刺史張懿、涼州刺史耿鄙並為寇賊所害，故焉議得用。
value.en: Before the reform could take effect, Yi Province's Inspector Xi Jian had drawn widespread complaint for his harsh rule, while the inspectors of Bing and Liang, Zhang Yi and Geng Bi, had both fallen to rebels—circumstances that finally won acceptance for Liu Yan's proposal.
value.literal: The proposal had not yet been carried out when Inspector Xi Jian of Yi Province proved vexatious in administration and rumors of it spread far; moreover Inspectors Zhang Yi of Bing and Geng Bi of Liang were both killed by bandits, so Yan's plan was adopted.

value.zh: 出焉為監軍使者，領益州牧，太僕黃琬為豫州牧，宗正劉虞為幽州牧，皆以本秩居職。
value.en: Liu Yan was named military overseer and shepherd of Yi Province, Huang Wan grand coachman and shepherd of Yu, and Liu Yu minister of the imperial clan and shepherd of You, each continuing at his former nominal grade.
value.literal: Yan was sent out as Military Overseer and Envoy and appointed shepherd of Yi Province; Grand Coachman Huang Wan became shepherd of Yu Province; Minister of the Imperial Clan Liu Yu became shepherd of You Province; each held office at his existing salary rank.

value.zh: 州任之重，自此而始。
value.en: From that moment the office of provincial shepherd carried real power.
value.literal: The weight of responsibility for a province began from this.

value.literal: Biographies 66: Virtuous Officials — Lu Kezhong, Niu Dechang, Fan Chengji, Wang Zheng, Zhang Yi, Li Zhan, Liu Minxing, Fu Shenwei, Liu Huan, Gao Changfu, Sun Deyuan, Zhao Jian, Pucha Zhengliu, Nuxilie Shouyu, Shi Moyuan, Zhang Gou, Zhao Zhongfu, Wu Dou, Geshilie De, Zhang Teli, Wang Hao

value.zh: 張奕，字彥微，其先澤州高平人。
value.en: Zhang Yi, styled Yanwei, traced his ancestry to Gaoping in Ze Prefecture.
value.literal: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Yanwei, was descended from Gaoping in Ze Prefecture.

value.zh: 以廕補官，仕齊為歸德府通判。
value.en: He entered office through hereditary privilege and served the Qi state as vice prefect of Guide Prefecture.
value.literal: He entered office through hereditary privilege and served Qi as vice prefect of Guide Prefecture.

value.zh: 齊國廢，齊兵之在郡者二萬人謀為亂，約夜半舉燎相應。
value.en: When the Qi state was abolished, the twenty thousand Qi troops still in the prefecture plotted a revolt, agreeing to light beacon fires at midnight as their signal.
value.literal: When the Qi state was abolished, the twenty thousand Qi soldiers in the prefecture plotted rebellion, agreeing to raise beacon fires at midnight as signals to one another.

value.zh: 奕知之，選市人丁壯授以兵，結陣扼其要巷，開小南門以示生路，亂不得作，比明亡匿略盡，擒其首惡誅之。
value.en: Yi learned of the plot, drafted able-bodied men from the market and armed them, formed ranks to hold the key alleys, and opened the Small South Gate to offer an escape route. The revolt never broke out; by dawn most of the conspirators had fled, and Yi seized the ringleaders and executed them.
value.literal: Yi learned of it, selected able-bodied men from the market and armed them, formed ranks to block the key alleys, and opened the Small South Gate to show an escape route. The rebellion could not break out; by dawn those in hiding had largely fled, and he seized the ringleaders and executed them.

value.zh: 後五日，都統完顏阿魯補以軍至歸德，欲根株餘黨，奕以闔門保郡人無他，遂止。
value.en: Five days later Commander Wanyan Alubu arrived at Guide with his army and wanted to root out every last conspirator. Yi pledged his entire household that the people of the prefecture meant no further harm, and the purge was stopped.
value.literal: Five days later the commander Wanyan Alubu arrived at Guide with his army and wished to root out the remaining conspirators. Yi pledged his entire household that the people of the prefecture had no further designs, and the pursuit was halted.

value.zh: 行台承制除同知歸德尹。
value.en: The mobile secretariat, acting under imperial commission, appointed him deputy prefect of Guide.
value.literal: The mobile secretariat, acting under imperial commission, appointed him deputy prefect of Guide.

value.zh: 天眷元年，以河南與宋，改同知沂州防禦使事。
value.en: In the first year of Tianjuan, when Henan was ceded to Song, he was made deputy defender of Yizhou.
value.literal: In the first year of Tianjuan, when Henan was ceded to Song, he was changed to deputy defender of Yizhou.

value.zh: 三年，宗弼複取河南，征奕赴行省，既定汴京，授汴京副留守。
value.en: In the third year Zongbi retook Henan; Yi was summoned to the mobile secretariat, and once Bianjing was secured he was made deputy guardian of Bianjing.
value.literal: In the third year Zongbi recovered Henan; Yi was summoned to the mobile secretariat, and once Bianjing was secured he was appointed deputy guardian of Bianjing.

value.zh: 曆陳、秦州防禦使，同知太原尹。
value.en: He successively served as defender of Chen and Qin prefectures and as deputy metropolitan prefect of Taiyuan.
value.literal: He successively served as defender of Chen and Qin prefectures and as deputy metropolitan prefect of Taiyuan.

value.zh: 晉甯軍報夏人侵界，詔奕往征之。
value.en: The Jinning Army reported a Xia border incursion; the throne ordered Yi to investigate.
value.literal: The Jinning Army reported that the Xia had invaded the border; an edict ordered Yi to go and investigate.

value.zh: 奕至境上，按籍各歸所侵土，還奏曰：「折氏世守麟府，以抗夏人。
value.en: Yi reached the border, checked the registers, and restored each tract of invaded land; on returning he memorialized, "The Zhe clan had held Lin Prefecture for generations to resist the Xia.
value.literal: Yi reached the border, checked the registers, and returned each tract of invaded land; returning he memorialized: "The Zhe clan for generations held Lin Prefecture to resist the Xia.

value.zh: 本朝有其地遂以與夏。
value.en: Our dynasty held that territory and then ceded it to the Xia.
value.literal: Our dynasty possessed that territory and then gave it to the Xia.

value.zh: 夏人夷折氏墳壟而戮其屍，折氏怨入骨髓而不得報也。
value.en: The Xia leveled the Zhe tombs and desecrated their dead; the Zhe clan's hatred ran to the marrow and could not be avenged.
value.literal: The Xia leveled the Zhe clan's tombs and desecrated their corpses; the Zhe clan's hatred entered to the marrow and could not be avenged.

value.zh: 今複使守晉寧，故激怒夏人使為鼠侵，而條上其罪，苟欲開邊釁以雪私仇耳。
value.en: Now they are posted again to guard Jinning, deliberately provoking petty Xia raids while charges are filed against them—this is only to open a border quarrel and settle a private grudge.
value.literal: Now they are again made to guard Jinning, so the Xia are deliberately provoked into petty incursions, and charges are listed against them—this is merely to open a border quarrel and settle a private grudge.

value.zh: 獨可徙折氏他郡，則夏人自安。」
value.en: Move the Zhe clan to another prefecture, and the Xia will settle down of themselves."
value.literal: They need only be moved to another prefecture, and the Xia will settle of themselves."

value.zh: 朝廷從之，遂移折氏守青州。
value.en: The court agreed and transferred the Zhe clan to guard Qingzhou.
value.literal: The court adopted this and thereupon transferred the Zhe clan to guard Qingzhou.

value.zh: 正隆間，同知西京留守事，遷河東北路轉運使。
value.en: During Zhenglong he served as deputy guardian of the Western Capital and was promoted to transport commissioner of the Hedong North Route.
value.literal: During the Zhenglong era he served as deputy guardian of the Western Capital and was promoted to transport commissioner of the Hedong North Route.

value.zh: 大定二年，征為戶部尚書，甫視事，得疾卒。
value.en: In the second year of Dading he was summoned as minister of revenue; he had barely taken office when he fell ill and died.
value.literal: In the second year of Dading he was summoned as minister of revenue; he had only just taken office when he fell ill and died.

value.zh: 景皇帝諱師，字子元，宣帝長子也。
value.en: Emperor Jing, whose personal name was Shi and courtesy name Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan of Jin.
value.literal: Emperor Jing, taboo name Shi, courtesy name Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan.

value.zh: 雅有風彩，沈毅多大略。
value.en: He carried himself with quiet distinction, steady and resolute, with a strategist’s breadth of mind.
value.literal: He had refined bearing and presence, was deep and resolute, and possessed great strategic vision.

value.zh: 少流美譽，與夏侯玄、何晏齊名。
value.en: While still young he was widely praised, and his name stood alongside those of Xiahou Xuan and He Yan.
value.literal: In youth he enjoyed a fine reputation, and was ranked with Xiahou Xuan and He Yan.

value.zh: 晏常稱曰：「惟幾也能成天下之務，司馬子元是也。」
value.en: He Yan used to say, "It takes someone who senses the moment before it turns to carry the weight of the realm—and that man is Sima Ziyuan."
value.literal: He Yan often declared, "Only one who apprehends subtle turning points can accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven; Sima Ziyuan is such a man."

value.zh: 魏景初中，拜散騎常侍，累遷中護軍。
value.en: During Wei’s Jingchu years he received appointment as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and rose step by step to Central Protector of the Army.
value.literal: In the Jingchu era of Wei, he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and eventually promoted to Central Protector of the Army.

value.zh: 為選用之法，舉不越功，吏無私焉。
value.en: He set rules for appointments so that promotions matched real achievement, and his staff could not trade on personal connections.
value.literal: He established methods for selection and appointment; recommendations did not exceed actual merit, and clerks practiced no private favoritism.

value.zh: 宣穆皇后崩，居喪以至孝聞。
value.en: After Empress Dowager Xuanmu’s death, he kept mourning with such scrupulous grief that word of his filial piety spread everywhere.
value.literal: When Empress Dowager Xuanmu died, he observed mourning for her and was famed for extreme filial devotion.

value.zh: 宣帝之將誅曹爽，深謀秘策，獨與帝潛畫，文帝弗之知也。
value.en: As Sima Yi readied the strike against Cao Shuang, he laid his plans in the deepest secrecy—working them out alone with Sima Shi—while Sima Zhao was kept entirely in the dark.
value.literal: When Emperor Xuan was about to execute Cao Shuang, with deep plots and secret stratagems he secretly planned only with the Emperor (Sima Shi); Emperor Wen (Sima Zhao) did not know of it.

value.zh: 將發夕乃告之，既而使人覘之，帝寢如常，而文帝不能安席。
value.en: Sima Yi waited until the night before the coup to inform his son; when he sent men to watch Sima Shi’s quarters, Shi slept soundly as on any other night, while Sima Zhao tossed and could not settle.
value.literal: On the eve of launching the action he was told; then someone was sent to spy on him—the Emperor slept as usual, but Emperor Wen could not find rest on his mat.

value.zh: 晨會兵司馬門，鎮靜內外，置陣甚整。
value.en: At daybreak he drew up his forces at the Sima Gate, steadying the palace inside and out and arraying them with flawless discipline.
value.literal: At dawn he assembled troops at the Sima Gate, calming inside and outside, and deployed formations in very good order.

value.zh: 宣帝曰：「此子竟可也。」
value.en: Sima Yi said, "This boy will do after all."
value.literal: Emperor Xuan said, "This son is indeed capable."

value.zh: 初，帝陰養死士三千，散在人間，至是一朝而集，眾莫知所出也。
value.en: Earlier, Sima Shi had quietly kept three thousand devoted fighters dispersed through the capital; now they materialized overnight, and no one could guess where they had sprung from.
value.literal: At the outset the Emperor had secretly maintained three thousand bravos, scattered among the people; at this moment they gathered in a single morning, and the multitude did not know whence they had come.

value.zh: 事平，以功封長平鄉侯，食邑千戶，尋加衛將軍。
value.en: After the coup succeeded he was rewarded with the village marquisate of Changping and a thousand-household fief, and before long was named General of the Guard as well.
value.literal: When the affair was settled, by merit he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Changping with a fief of one thousand households; soon he was additionally appointed General of the Guard.

value.zh: 及宣帝薨，議者咸云「伊尹既卒，伊陟嗣事」，天子命帝以撫軍大將軍輔政。
value.en: At Sima Yi’s death, court opinion echoed the old line—“When Yi Yin passed away, his son Yi Zhi carried on the task”—and the Wei emperor appointed Sima Shi General Who Pacifies the Army to assist in government.
value.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, those who deliberated all said, "After Yi Yin died, Yi Zhi succeeded to his duties," and the Son of Heaven ordered the Emperor as General Who Stabilizes the Army and Great General to assist in government.

value.zh: 魏嘉平四年春正月，遷大將軍，加侍中，持節、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事。
value.en: In the first month of spring, Wei’s fourth year of Jiaping, he advanced to Great General, was given the concurrent post of Palace Attendant, received the imperial baton, took overall command of central and frontier forces, and assumed control of the Secretariat.
value.literal: In the first month of spring in the fourth year of Jiaping of Wei, he was promoted to Great General, added as Palace Attendant, bearing credentials, supervising all military affairs of the central command and the regions, and recording Director of the Secretariat business.

value.zh: 命百官舉賢才，明少長，恤窮獨，理廢滯。
value.en: He instructed every office to put forward able men, to sort seniority fairly, to relieve the widowed and alone, and to clear the backlog of neglected business.
value.literal: He ordered the hundred officials to recommend worthy talent, clarify precedence of young and old, show pity to the destitute and solitary, and straighten out stalled appointments.

value.zh: 諸葛誕、毌丘儉、王昶、陳泰、胡遵都督四方，王基、州泰、鄧艾、石苞典州郡，盧毓、李豐裳選舉，傅嘏、虞松參計謀，鐘會、夏侯玄、王肅、陳本、孟康、趙酆、張緝預朝議，四海傾注，朝野肅然。
value.en: Zhuge Dan, Guanqiu Jian, Wang Chang, Chen Tai, and Hu Zun held regional commands; Wang Ji, Zhou Tai, Deng Ai, and Shi Bao ran the provinces; Lu Yu and Li Feng handled personnel; Fu Gu and Yu Song shaped policy; Zhong Hui, Xiahou Xuan, Wang Su, Chen Ben, Meng Kang, Zhao Feng, and Zhang Ji sat in on the great councils. The empire fixed its hopes on them, and court and countryside grew solemn.
value.literal: Zhuge Dan, Guanqiu Jian, Wang Chang, Chen Tai, and Hu Zun supervised the four quarters; Wang Ji, Zhou Tai, Deng Ai, and Shi Bao administered prefectures and commanderies; Lu Yu and Li Feng oversaw selection and appointment; Fu Gu and Yu Song joined in planning stratagems; Zhong Hui, Xiahou Xuan, Wang Su, Chen Ben, Meng Kang, Zhao Feng, and Zhang Ji took part in court deliberations; the four seas turned their gaze upon them, and court and countryside stood in solemn awe.

value.zh: 或有請改易制度者，帝曰：「'不識不知，順帝之則'，詩人之美也。
value.en: When voices rose for sweeping institutional change, Sima Shi answered, "The Odes praise the ruler who does not meddle for show but simply follows the pattern Heaven set for the sage-kings.
value.literal: When some requested changes to institutions, the Emperor said: "'Not knowing, not perceiving, following the norms of the Di'—that is what the poets praise.

value.zh: 三祖典制，所宜遵奉；
value.en: The precedents left by the three Wei founders are what we are bound to honor;
value.literal: The regulations of the three founding ancestors are what ought to be obeyed and upheld;

value.zh: 自非軍事，不得妄有改革。」
value.en: and apart from what war demands, nothing should be changed on a whim."
value.literal: unless it be military affairs, one must not recklessly carry out reforms."

value.zh: 二年春正月，有彗星見於吳楚之分，西北竟天。
value.en: In the first month of spring, the second year, a comet blazed across the Wu–Chu sector of the sky from the northwest to the horizon.
value.literal: In the second year, spring, first month, there was a comet appearing in the Wu-Chu division, in the northwest filling the sky.

value.zh: 鎮東大將軍毌丘儉、揚州刺史文欽舉兵作亂，矯太后令移檄郡國，為壇盟於西門之外，各遣子四人質于吳以請救。
value.en: Guanqiu Jian, Grand General Who Guards the East, and Wen Qin, Yangzhou’s inspector, rose in revolt, forged a rescript in the Dowager’s name, sent manifestos across the commanderies, swore a blood oath on a platform west of the walls, and each sent four sons east as hostages to beg Wu for aid.
value.literal: General Who Guards the East Guanqiu Jian and Inspector of Yangzhou Wen Qin raised troops and made rebellion, falsely issuing an empress dowager order and circulating proclamations through commanderies and principalities; they made an altar covenant outside the west gate, each sending four sons as hostages to Wu to request rescue.

value.zh: 二月，儉、欽帥眾六萬，渡淮而西。
value.en: In the second month they marched sixty thousand men across the Huai and drove west.
value.literal: In the second month, Jian and Qin led a host of sixty thousand, crossed the Huai and went west.

value.zh: 帝會公卿謀征討計，朝議多謂可遣諸將擊之，王肅及尚書傅嘏、中書侍郎鐘會勸帝自行。
value.en: Sima Shi called the high ministers to plan the campaign; most favored sending subordinate generals, but Wang Su, Fu Gu of the Secretariat, and Zhong Hui of the Palace Secretariat pressed him to take the field himself.
value.literal: The Emperor convened dukes and ministers to plan punitive expedition strategy; court deliberation mostly said one could dispatch various generals to strike them, but Wang Su and Director of the Secretariat Fu Gu and Palace Secretariat Gentleman Zhong Hui urged the Emperor to go in person.

value.zh: 戊午，帝統中軍步騎十餘萬以征之。
value.en: On wuwu he led well over a hundred thousand central-army horse and foot against the rebels.
value.literal: On wuwu, the Emperor commanded the central army infantry and cavalry of more than one hundred thousand to campaign against them.

value.zh: 倍道兼行，召三方兵，大會于陳許之郊。
value.en: He forced the march, called in contingents from three directions, and massed them on the Chen–Xu plain.
value.literal: Doubling roads and marching together, he summoned troops from three directions and held a great assembly on the outskirts of Chen and Xu.

value.zh: 甲申，次於隱橋，儉將史招、李績相次來降。
value.en: On jiashen he encamped at Yinqiao, where Jian’s officers Shi Zhao and Li Ji surrendered in quick succession.
value.literal: On jiashen, he halted at Yinqiao; Jian's generals Shi Zhao and Li Ji came to surrender one after another.

value.zh: 儉、欽移入項城，帝遣荊州刺史王基進據南頓以逼儉。
value.en: When the rebels pulled into Xiangcheng, Sima Shi ordered Jingzhou Inspector Wang Ji to seize Nandun and pin Jian in place.
value.literal: Jian and Qin shifted into Xiangcheng; the Emperor sent Inspector of Jingzhou Wang Ji to advance and occupy Nandun in order to press Jian.

value.zh: 帝深壁高壘，以待東軍之集。
value.en: He dug in behind high walls and waited for the eastern columns to assemble.
value.literal: The Emperor deepened walls and raised high ramparts, in order to await the gathering of eastern troops.

value.zh: 諸將請進軍攻其城，帝曰：「諸君得其一，未知其二。
value.en: The generals requested advancing the army to attack the city. Sima Shi said, "You gentlemen have grasped one point, but do not yet know the second.
value.literal: The generals requested advancing the army to attack the city. Sima Shi said, "You gentlemen have grasped one point, but do not yet know the second.

value.zh: 淮南將士本無反志。
value.en: The Huainan rank and file never wanted this rebellion.
value.literal: The Huainan officers and soldiers fundamentally had no rebellious intent.

value.zh: 且儉、欽欲蹈縱橫之跡，習儀秦之說，謂遠近必應。
value.en: Jian and Wen Qin fancy themselves wandering strategists in the mold of Su Qin and Zhang Yi; they expect the whole region to rise at their call.
value.literal: Moreover Jian and Qin wish to tread the traces of the vertical-horizontal persuaders, practice the doctrines of Yi and Qin, and think that near and far will surely respond.

value.zh: 而事起之日，淮北不從，史招、李績前後瓦解。
value.en: When the revolt broke, the north bank of the Huai refused to move, and Shi Zhao and Li Ji melted away in turn.
value.literal: Yet on the day the affair arose, north of the Huai they did not follow; Shi Zhao and Li Ji before and after disintegrated.

value.zh: 內乖外叛，自知必敗，困獸思鬥，速戰更合其志。
value.en: Betrayed within and without, they know they are finished; like beasts at bay they will fight—and a hasty battle is exactly what they want.
value.literal: Inner discord and outer rebellion—they know themselves they must be defeated; a cornered beast thinks of fighting; swift battle further fits their intent.

value.zh: 雖云必克，傷人亦多。
value.en: We might win a rush attack, but the butcher’s bill would be steep.
value.literal: Although it is said one must surely overcome, the wounded will also be many.

value.zh: 且儉等欺誑將士，詭變萬端，小與持久，詐情自露，此不戰而克之也。」
value.en: Moreover, Guanqiu Jian and the others deceive and mislead their officers and soldiers, changing deceitfully in a myriad ways. Stay with them a little longer, and their fraudulent situation will reveal itself; this is conquering them without battle."
value.literal: Moreover, Guanqiu Jian and the others deceive and mislead their officers and soldiers, changing deceitfully in a myriad ways. Stay with them a little longer, and their fraudulent situation will reveal itself; this is conquering them without battle."

value.zh: 乃遣諸葛誕督豫州諸軍自安風向壽春，征東將軍胡遵督青、徐諸軍出譙宋之間，絕其歸路。
value.en: He sent Zhuge Dan with the Yu columns from Anfeng toward Shouchun and Hu Zun with Qing–Xu forces through the Qiao–Song corridor to sever their retreat.
value.literal: Thereupon he dispatched Zhuge Dan to supervise Yu Province troops from Anfeng toward Shouchun, and General Who Conquers the East Hu Zun to supervise Qing and Xu troops out between Qiao and Song, cutting off their return route.

value.zh: 帝屯汝陽，遣競州刺史鄧艾督太山諸軍進屯樂嘉，示弱以誘之。
value.en: Sima Shi camped at Ruyang and ordered Yanzhou Inspector Deng Ai to push the Taishan contingents forward to Lejia and feign weakness as bait.
value.literal: The Emperor encamped at Ruyang and sent Inspector of Yan Province Deng Ai to supervise Taishan troops to advance and encamp at Lejia, showing weakness in order to lure them.

value.zh: 欽進軍將攻艾，帝潛軍銜枚，輕造樂嘉，與欽相遇。
value.en: When Wen Qin advanced on Deng Ai, Sima Shi slipped an army forward with bits in the horses’ mouths, raced to Lejia, and met Wen Qin head-on.
value.literal: Qin advanced the army about to attack Ai; the Emperor secretly moved troops with mouth-gags, lightly went to Lejia, and encountered Qin.

value.zh: 欽子鴦，年十八，勇冠三軍，謂欽曰：「及其未定，請登城鼓噪，擊之可破也。」
value.en: Qin's son Yang was eighteen, and his courage topped the three armies. He said to Qin, "Before they are settled, please climb the wall, beat the drums, and shout; attacking them can break them."
value.literal: Qin's son Yang was eighteen, and his courage topped the three armies. He said to Qin, "Before they are settled, please climb the wall, beat the drums, and shout; attacking them can break them."

value.zh: 既謀而行，三噪而欽不能應，鴦退，相與引而東。
value.en: They put the plan in motion, but after three rounds of shouting Wen Qin never moved; Yang fell back, and father and son drew off toward the east.
value.literal: Having planned then acting, three clamors yet Qin could not respond; Yang withdrew, together they led away eastward.

value.zh: 帝謂諸將曰：「欽走矣。」
value.en: Sima Shi told the generals, "Qin has fled."
value.literal: Sima Shi told the generals, "Qin has fled."

value.zh: 命發銳軍以追之。
value.en: He ordered the elite vanguard forward in pursuit.
value.literal: He ordered to dispatch picked troops to pursue them.

value.zh: 諸將皆曰：「欽舊將，鴦少而銳，引軍內入，未有失利，必不走也。」
value.en: The generals all said, "Qin is an old general, and Yang is young and sharp. They led the army deep inside and have not yet suffered defeat; they surely will not flee."
value.literal: The generals all said, "Qin is an old general, and Yang is young and sharp. They led the army deep inside and have not yet suffered defeat; they surely will not flee."

value.zh: 帝曰：「一鼓作氣，再而衰，三而竭。
value.en: Sima Shi said, "With one drumbeat, spirit rises; with the second it declines; with the third it is exhausted.
value.literal: Sima Shi said, "With one drumbeat, spirit rises; with the second it declines; with the third it is exhausted.

value.zh: 鴦三鼓，欽不應，其勢已屈，不走何待？」
value.en: Yang beat the drum three times, and Qin did not respond; their force is already bent. If they do not flee, what are they waiting for?"
value.literal: Yang beat the drum three times, and Qin did not respond; their force is already bent. If they do not flee, what are they waiting for?"

value.zh: 欽將遁，鴦曰：「不先折其勢，不得去也。」
value.en: When Qin was about to flee, Yang said, "If we do not first break their force, we cannot leave."
value.literal: When Qin was about to flee, Yang said, "If we do not first break their force, we cannot leave."

value.zh: 乃與驍騎十餘摧鋒陷陣，所向皆披靡，遂引去。
value.en: He led a dozen picked horsemen in a spearhead charge that scattered every line before him, then broke off and withdrew.
value.literal: Then with more than ten swift cavalry he shattered the vanguard and broke formations; wherever he went all were swept aside; then he led away.

value.zh: 帝遣左長史司馬璉督驍騎八千翼而追之，使將軍樂林等督步兵繼其後。
value.en: Sima Shi sent his left chief clerk Sima Lian with eight thousand horse to sweep around Wen Qin’s flank and told generals such as Yue Lin to bring the footsoldiers up behind.
value.literal: The Emperor sent Left Chief Clerk Sima Lian to supervise eight thousand swift cavalry to flank and pursue them, and ordered generals such as Yue Lin to supervise infantry to follow their rear.

value.zh: 比至沙陽，頻陷欽陣，弩矢雨下，欽蒙盾而馳。
value.en: By Shayang they had torn through Wen Qin’s lines again and again; bolts fell like rain, and Wen Qin crouched under his shield and spurred on.
value.literal: By the time they reached Shayang, repeatedly they broke Qin's formations; crossbow bolts rained down; Qin covered himself with a shield and galloped.

value.zh: 大破其軍。
value.en: They shattered his army.
value.literal: Greatly defeated his army.

value.zh: 眾皆投戈而降，欽父子與麾下走保項。
value.en: The men threw down their weapons and yielded; Wen Qin and his son raced with their remaining followers to the refuge of Xiang.
value.literal: The host all cast aside halberds and surrendered; Qin father and son with those under their command fled to protect Xiang.

value.zh: 儉聞欽敗，棄眾宵遁淮南。
value.en: Guanqiu Jian, hearing of Wen Qin’s rout, abandoned his army and fled south into Huainan by night.
value.literal: When Jian heard Qin was defeated, he abandoned the host and fled by night to Huainan.

value.zh: 安風津都尉追儉，斬之，傳首京都。
value.en: The commandant at Anfeng Ford ran him down, struck off his head, and sent it to the capital by post-horse.
value.literal: The Commandant of Anfeng Ford pursued Jian, beheaded him, and sent the head by relay to the capital.

value.zh: 欽遂奔吳，淮南平。
value.en: Wen Qin escaped into Wu, and the Huainan rebellion was over.
value.literal: Qin then fled to Wu; Huainan was pacified.

value.zh: 刑法志
value.en: Monograph: Criminal Law.
value.literal: Treatise on Punishment and Law.

value.zh: 及帝即位，展為廷尉，又上言：「古者肉刑，事經前聖，漢文除之，增加大辟。
value.en: When the emperor came to the throne, Wei Zhan became Commandant of Justice and again submitted words: "In antiquity, corporal punishments were matters passed through former sages; Emperor Wen of Han abolished them and increased capital penalties.
value.literal: When the emperor came to the throne, Wei Zhan became Commandant of Justice and again submitted words: "In antiquity, corporal punishments were matters passed through former sages; Emperor Wen of Han abolished them and increased capital penalties.

value.zh: 今人戶凋荒，百不遺一，而刑法峻重，非句踐養胎之義也。
value.en: Depopulation clashes with Goujian-style mercy.
value.literal: Now households are devastated—not one in a hundred survives—yet punishments stay harsh—this is not Goujian’s nurture-the-womb kindness.

value.zh: 愚謂宜復古施行，以隆太平之化。」
value.en: I foolishly think it fitting to restore antiquity and put it into effect, in order to exalt the transformation of Great Peace."
value.literal: I foolishly think it fitting to restore antiquity and put it into effect, in order to exalt the transformation of Great Peace."

value.zh: 詔內外通議。
value.en: Court-wide deliberation ensued.
value.literal: Edict ordered inner and outer courts deliberate.

value.zh: 於是驃騎將軍王導、太常賀循、侍中紀瞻、中書郎庾亮、大將軍諮議參軍梅陶、散騎郎張嶷等議，以：「肉刑之典，由來尚矣。
value.en: Thereupon General of Agile Cavalry Wang Dao, Chamberlain for Ceremonials He Xun, Attendant Ji Zhan, Palace Writer Gentleman Yu Liang, Great General's Advisory Army Consultant Mei Tao, Cavalier Gentleman Zhang Yi, and others deliberated, saying: "The canon of corporal punishments has long been honored in origin.
value.literal: Thereupon General of Agile Cavalry Wang Dao, Chamberlain for Ceremonials He Xun, Attendant Ji Zhan, Palace Writer Gentleman Yu Liang, Great General's Advisory Army Consultant Mei Tao, Cavalier Gentleman Zhang Yi, and others deliberated, saying: "The canon of corporal punishments has long been honored in origin.

value.zh: 肇自古先，以及三代，聖哲明王所未曾改也。
value.en: Three-age kings kept mutilation.
value.literal: From earliest ancestors through three dynasties sagely enlightened kings never altered them.

value.zh: 豈是漢文常主所能易者乎！
value.en: Han Wendi was no sage legislator.
value.literal: How could mere Emperor Wen of Han alter them!

value.zh: 時蕭曹已沒，絳灌之徒不能正其義。
value.en: Early Han lacked wise ministers to defend classical law.
value.literal: At that time Xiao He and Cao Shen had died—subordinates like Zhou Bo could not straighten principle.

value.zh: 逮班固深論其事，以為外有輕刑之名，內實殺人。
value.en: Ban Gu exposed Wen’s reform as bloodier.
value.literal: When Ban Gu examined deeply he judged outwardly lighter punishments inwardly killed more.

value.zh: 又死刑太重，生刑太輕，生刑縱於上，死刑怨於下，輕重失當，故刑政不中也。
value.en: Wen’s imbalance caused penal dysfunction.
value.literal: Further capital death weighs too heavy while living punishments weigh too light—living lax above, capital bitter below—imbalance misorders punishments.

value.zh: 且原先王之造刑也，非以過怒也，非以殘人也，所以救奸，所以當罪。
value.en: Classical mutilation targeted rehabilitation.
value.literal: Moreover former kings crafting punishments acted not from excess anger nor desire to maim but to rescue society and match guilt.

value.zh: 今盜者竊人之財，淫者好人之色，亡者避叛之役，皆無殺害也，則加之以刑。
value.en: Non-capital crimes received death.
value.literal: Now thieves steal lust seduces fugitives flee corvée—none kills yet punishments apply.

value.zh: 刑之則止，而加之斬戮，戮過其罪，死不可生，縱虐於此，歲以巨計。
value.en: Death sentences overshot proportion annually.
value.literal: Punishment should stop yet waist-cutting adds killing—execution exceeds guilt—death cannot revive—such cruelty yearly tallies vast.

value.zh: 此乃仁人君子所不忍聞，而況行之於政乎！
value.en: Mass execution horrifies humane ears.
value.literal: This benevolent gentlemen cannot bear hearing—how execute policy!

value.zh: 若乃惑其名而不練其實，惡其生而趣其死，此畏水投舟，避坎蹈井，愚夫之不若，何取於政哉！
value.en: Rejecting mutilation for killing is suicidal stupidity.
value.literal: If deluded by reputation ignoring substance hating life rushing death—that fears water yet boards boat avoids pit yet leaps well—fools exceed such conduct—what governance values that!

value.zh: 今大晉中興，遵復古典，率由舊章，起千載之滯義，拯百殘之遺黎，使皇典廢而復存，黔首死而更生，至義暢於三代之際，遺風播乎百世之後，生肉枯骨，惠侔造化，豈不休哉！
value.en: Now in the Great Jin Restoration, the dynasty follows and restores the ancient canons and is guided by the old regulations. It raises up a meaning stalled for a thousand years, rescues the surviving people from a hundred ruins, makes the imperial canon exist again after being abolished, and makes the common people live again after death. Utmost righteousness will flourish in the age of the Three Dynasties, and its remaining influence will spread after a hundred generations. To make flesh grow on dry bones and make kindness equal to creation: is this not excellent!
value.literal: Now in the Great Jin Restoration, the dynasty follows and restores the ancient canons and is guided by the old regulations. It raises up a meaning stalled for a thousand years, rescues the surviving people from a hundred ruins, makes the imperial canon exist again after being abolished, and makes the common people live again after death. Utmost righteousness will flourish in the age of the Three Dynasties, and its remaining influence will spread after a hundred generations. To make flesh grow on dry bones and make kindness equal to creation: is this not excellent!

value.zh: 惑者乃曰，死猶不懲，而況于刑？
value.en: Skeptics ask whether mutilation deters.
value.literal: Critics say death still fails to deter—how much less mutilation?

value.zh: 然人者冥也，其至愚矣，雖加斬戮，忽為灰土，死事日往，生欲日存，未以為改。
value.en: Death’s abstraction fails deterrence.
value.literal: Yet humans are benighted—most foolish—even executions vanish them to ash daily death dulls desire—few reform.

value.zh: 若刑諸市朝，朝夕鑒戒，刑者詠為惡之永痛，惡者睹殘刖之長廢，故足懼也。
value.en: Public mutilation educates better than hidden execution.
value.literal: If executing in marketplace morning and evening offers mirror—criminals chant wicked pain forever villains glimpse lifelong maiming—then awe suffices.

value.zh: 然後知先王之輕刑以禦物，顯誡以懲愚，其理遠矣。」
value.en: Only then do we know that the former kings used light punishments to govern things and visible admonitions to discipline the foolish; their principle was far-reaching."
value.literal: Only then do we know that the former kings used light punishments to govern things and visible admonitions to discipline the foolish; their principle was far-reaching."

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。
value.en: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.
value.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.

value.zh: 以劉寔為師，孟珩為友，楊准、馮蓀為文學。
value.en: Liu Shi served as tutor, Meng Heng as companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun as literary aides.
value.literal: Liu Shi was made tutor, Meng Heng companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun literary aides.

value.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇太子。
value.en: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.

value.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。
value.en: The court recruited eminent tutors—He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
value.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

value.zh: 元康元年，出就東宮，又詔曰：「遹尚幼蒙，今出東宮，惟當賴師傅群賢之訓。
value.en: In Yuankang year one he moved to the Eastern Palace, and an edict declared: "Yu is still young and inexperienced; now that he has moved to the Eastern Palace he must rely on his tutors and worthy mentors for instruction.
value.literal: In the first year of Yuankang he moved out to the Eastern Palace; an edict further said: "Yu is still young and untutored; now that he is moving out to the Eastern Palace he should rely solely on the instruction of his tutors and the worthy assembly.

value.zh: 其遊處左右，宜得正人使共周旋，能相長益者。」
value.en: Those about him in leisure and attendance should be upright men who keep company with him and help one another improve."
value.literal: Those who attend him in leisure and service should be upright men who may keep company with him and mutually aid one another's growth."

value.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。
value.en: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.
value.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.

value.zh: 序
value.en: Preface
